packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
PACKET-01 - UNVERIFIED IMAGE-ONLY READING

Exposure statement: Nothing in my context proposed an identification or reading of these images. My session context (a personal-assistant memory index) mentions in general terms that the user works on manuscript-fragment identification projects, but it names no work, author, text or reading for this packet. I did nothing beyond the stated rules, except that I listed the two packet directories (file names only) and checked image pixel sizes with a shell command so I could see which files were overviews and which were tiles. I did not open packet.json.

Conventions: ( ) = proposed expansion of an abbreviation; ? after a word = uncertain reading; [illegible] = not read; ] at line start = text lost/cropped to the left; [ at line end = text lost/cropped to the right. "ke" renders the k-with-stroke abbreviation (ke/que); "p(ur)" renders p with superscript o-like mark; "g(ra)nt" renders g with superscript mark.

======================================================================
LAYOUT SURVEY (observations)
======================================================================
Four overviews = four faces of a parchment fragment (or of two fragments of the same book): image-001, image-006, image-011, image-016. Each is followed by four native tiles (2 x 2 grid, overlapping): upper-left, upper-right, lower-left, lower-right.

Common features:
- Fragment about 9 cm wide x 14 cm high (ruler in frame). Upright orientation.
- Two columns of short lines, one line per short line of text (looks like verse: lines of roughly 8 syllables, many rhyming in pairs, e.g. -er/-er, -eyt/-eyt, -unt/-ant). Each line begins with a capital or enlarged letter.
- Faint vertical ruling between columns. No running title visible (top margin trimmed).
- Single gothic book hand, vernacular (French-type) language. Common abbreviations: k-with-stroke (ke), p with superscript (pur), superscript-marked g(ra)nt, Qnt with bar (quant), macron for nasal.
- No interlinear or marginal glosses seen.
- In every face one column is complete in width and the other is cut so only line beginnings or line ends survive. Bottom lines on several faces are cropped or stained.
- Face image-011 has a red rubric line and a large red initial L (about 6 lines tall) in column b.
- Face image-016, column b: lines 2-3 are indented (start further right than the other lines); no initial is painted in the space.
- Face image-001: the left edge has a folded/turned strip (stub), and the right column is cut through mid-line.
- Face image-006: heavy brown staining on the left column and along the bottom; lower lines very hard to read.

Interpretation (tentative): continuous narrative/didactic verse about an angel, a soul (alme), devils and pains of the damned, then (image-016) the soul's arrival in a place of joy. I make no claim about author, work, date or provenance.
